name: Eri
overview: Eri was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known primarily as the son of Gad. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking his place in the early genealogical records of the Israelite people. His descendants, the Erites, are also mentioned, indicating the establishment of a familial line within the tribe of Gad.
namesAndTitles: The name Eri is a proper name meaning 'watcher,' as recorded in Genesis 46:16. This meaning, while noted, is not explicitly stated to have been given by God but reflects a Hebrew personal name of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eri as the son of Gad, establishing his direct paternal lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical record provided.
scriptureSignificance: Eri's significance in Scripture lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, a foundational event in the history of Israel's formation as a nation. His position as a son of Gad connects him to one of the twelve tribes, underscoring the tribal divisions that shape much of Israel's identity. The mention of the Erites as his descendants further emphasizes his role in the genealogical and tribal structure of Israel.
